bib.title: Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python
bib.venue: Journal of Machine Learning Research 12 (2011) 2825-2830 (arXiv v4, 2018)

question: How can a general-purpose high-level language library offer state-of-the-art machine learning to non-specialists with a consistent API and competitive speed?
hypothesis: A Python library built on numpy/scipy with compiled cores can be both easy to use and as fast as or faster than other Python ML toolkits.
contributions: A BSD-licensed Python module integrating many supervised and unsupervised algorithms for medium-scale problems
A consistent estimator/transformer/cross-validation-iterator API with GridSearchCV and Pipeline
A timing comparison against five Python ML libraries on Madelon

method.summary: Describes the design of scikit-learn (estimator interface, model selection, Pipeline) and times six algorithms against mlpy, pybrain, pymvpa, mdp and shogun on the Madelon data set.

datasets.name: Madelon
datasets.source: Guyon et al., 2004 (NIPS 2003 feature selection challenge)

models.name: scikit-learn
models.architecture: Python library over numpy, scipy, Cython; wraps LibSVM and LibLinear

metrics.name: Time
metrics.definition: computation time per algorithm on Madelon (what is timed, fit only or fit+predict, is not stated)

eval.protocol: Single table of times; no repeats, hardware, library versions, hyperparameters or algorithm settings stated beyond 9 PCA components and 9 k-means clusters; further benchmarks referred to github.

results.claim: Scikit-learn's SVC takes 5.2 s on Madelon, the lowest in the row; the next fastest is shogun at 5.63 s.
results.setup: Madelon, 4400x500; seconds; hardware and settings unstated.
results.table: Table 1, row Support Vector Classification, column scikit-learn
results.note: baseline_value is shogun; mlpy 9.47, pybrain 17.5, pymvpa 11.52, mdp 40.48

results.claim: Scikit-learn LARS Lasso takes 1.17 s versus 105.3 s for mlpy.
Elastic Net takes 0.52 s in scikit-learn versus 1.44 s in pymvpa and 73.7 s in mlpy.
results.table: Table 1, row Elastic Net, column scikit-learn

results.claim: k-NN takes 0.57 s in scikit-learn, essentially tied with pymvpa 0.56 s; mlpy 1.41.
results.table: Table 1, row k-Nearest Neighbors, column scikit-learn
results.note: baseline_value is pymvpa, which is slightly faster

results.claim: PCA with 9 components takes 0.18 s in scikit-learn versus 0.33 s shogun and 8.93 s pymvpa.
results.table: Table 1, row PCA (9 components), column scikit-learn

results.claim: k-means with 9 clusters takes 1.34 s in scikit-learn, slower than mlpy (0.79) and shogun (0.68).
results.table: Table 1, row k-Means (9 clusters), column scikit-learn
results.note: paper attributes this to pure-Python implementation and numpy multiple passes over data; pybrain does not converge within 1 hour

results.claim: Pipeline combines transformers and an estimator into one estimator so GridSearchCV tunes the parameters of all steps.
results.setup: Design description; the paper's only treatment of pipelines, with dimension reduction before fitting as the single example.
results.quote: Finally, a Pipeline object can combine several transformers and an estimator to create

results.claim: Estimators are defined by interface (fit, predict, transform, score), not inheritance.
Scikit-learn bindings to libsvm avoid memory copies and have up to 40% less overhead than the original libsvm Python bindings.
results.quote: up to 40% less overhead than the original libsvm Python bindings

results.claim: LARS gains 2-10 times over the reference R implementation.
results.setup: Versus Hastie and Efron 2004 R lars; no setup given.
results.quote: performance gains of 2–10 times over the reference R implementation

limits: Timing only; no accuracy comparison, no hardware, versions, repeats or settings stated.
Elastic Net: performance on very large problems is limited since no KKT active set is used.
k-means is pure Python and limited by numpy's multiple passes.
Targets medium-scale problems; online learning for large data sets is future work.
Table 1 is a 2011 snapshot; the library has changed greatly.

terms.definition: Estimators that implement a transform method, returning modified input data (e.g. PCA)
The central object; implements a fit method, accepting as arguments an input data array and optionally an array of labels
Provides pairs of train and test indices to split input data
